title: 01. Foundations: Agent Memory Types
summary: Agent memory encompasses all mechanisms by which an agent stores and retrieves information across time.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Agent memory encompasses all mechanisms by which an agent stores and retrieves information across time. There are five distinct memory types, each serving a different purpose: **In-context (short-term)** memory is the raw message history within the current context window — fast but limited by token budget. **External (long-term)** memory persists beyond the context window in vector stores, key-value databases, or graph databases. **Episodic memory** stores specific past interactions and their outcomes, enabling the agent to recall "what happened when I did X last time." **Semantic memory** holds structured world knowledge (facts, concepts) that the agent can query. **Procedural memory** encodes learned workflows and tool-use patterns — how the agent knows which steps to take for recurring task types. Production agents typically combine all five: in-context for the current turn, external + episodic for cross-session recall, semantic for domain knowledge, and procedural for task patterns.

diagrams.title: Agent memory types
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Q["New user message"] --> STM["Short-term - messages in this thread"]
  Q --> R{"Need older knowledge?"}
  R -- "facts about user" --> SEM[("Semantic - profile, preferences")]
  R -- "what happened before" --> EPI[("Episodic - past sessions, outcomes")]
  R -- "how to do it" --> PRO[("Procedural - instructions, skills")]
  STM --> CTX["Context window"]
  SEM --> CTX
  EPI --> CTX
  PRO --> CTX
  CTX --> LLM["LLM"]
diagrams.explain: **Short-term memory** is just the message list for the current thread — it lives in the context window and is lost when the thread ends. **Long-term memory** is stored outside the model and *retrieved* into the context when relevant: semantic (facts), episodic (past experiences) and procedural (how-to instructions). Everything the model "remembers" must end up in the context window.

sections.body:
```
AGENT MEMORY ARCHITECTURE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

                         AGENT BRAIN (LLM)
                               │
                    reads/writes during loop
                               │
        ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
        │                      │                      │
        ▼                      ▼                      ▼
┌──────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
│  IN-CONTEXT  │    │  VECTOR STORE   │    │   KEY-VALUE DB   │
│  (Short-term)│    │  (Long-term /   │    │  (Semantic       │
│              │    │   Semantic)     │    │   Memory)        │
│ Messages[]   │    │ FAISS / Pinecone│    │ Redis / DynamoDB │
│ ~128K tokens │    │ ~∞ documents    │    │ fact:value pairs │
│ Fast: O(1)   │    │ Semantic search │    │ Exact lookup     │
│ Ephemeral    │    │ Persistent      │    │ Persistent       │
└──────────────┘    └─────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘

┌──────────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────┐
│  EPISODIC MEMORY │              │  PROCEDURAL MEMORY     │
│                  │              │                        │
│ Past task runs:  │              │ Learned workflows:     │
│  - What happened │              │  - "For stock reports: │
│  - What worked   │              │    1. fetch prices     │
│  - What failed   │              │    2. calc metrics     │
│  Redis/Postgres  │              │    3. write report"    │
│  Indexed by      │              │  Stored as templates   │
│  task similarity │              │  Updated via feedback  │
└──────────────────┘              └────────────────────────┘

RETRIEVAL STRATEGIES:
═════════════════════
Similarity ──► Vector cosine search (semantic relevance)
Recency   ──► Timestamp-sorted (recent = more important)
Importance ──► Score-weighted (user-marked or LLM-scored)
Hybrid    ──► weighted_score = 0.5*sim + 0.3*recency + 0.2*importance
```

quiz.question: Implement all five memory types in a unified agent memory system.
options: stateless** — it takes input, returns output, and forgets everything.
The context window is the agent's working memory limit. Every message (system prompt + conversation + tool results) consumes tokens.
